technical_spec:
## M3.1.5 — GPU-resident kernel-only timing METHODOLOGY (honest scope)

### Scope statement (HONESTY-1)

The deliverable is the **resident-timing methodology**: upload weights/inputs to device-local VRAM ONCE, dispatch N times, and time only the GPU-side dispatch span (TOP→BOTTOM timestamp), EXCLUDING host upload/readback. This proves the M3.0 re-scoped claim that resident dispatch is fast. It is measured on EXISTING, already-correctness-verified kernels (saxpy, q4km matvec/matmul, coopmat matmul_tile) reporting kernel-only nanoseconds.

**OUT OF SCOPE:** a competitive 4096² matmul TFLOPS headline number. A real tiled/coalesced matmul needs `shared[T,N]` workgroup memory (FG.6) and is **M3.2**. The naive un-tiled scalar GEMM (`matmul_f32_tiled`) is used ONLY for harness validation and is labeled as such everywhere it appears — it is NOT presented as AXIOM-Compute's matmul performance.

### Timing semantics (TIMING-1, honest)

The measured quantity is the **GPU dispatch duration**: `vkCmdWriteTimestamp(TOP_OF_PIPE, q0)` recorded before the bind/dispatch and `vkCmdWriteTimestamp(BOTTOM_OF_PIPE, q1)` after the dispatch, within the SAME reusable CB. This span:
- EXCLUDES host upload (one-time, before the loop) and readback (after the loop) — THIS is the value vs dispatch_handle.
- INCLUDES dispatch launch + pipeline latency / drain. It is NOT isolated ALU time; do NOT call it 'kernel-only ALU'. Doc/prose say 'GPU dispatch duration (submit-to-completion timestamp span covering the single dispatch)'.

**Warmup-discard is MANDATORY:** discard the first 2 dispatch_resident measurements (pipeline warm-up, first-touch device-local page-in, clock ramp), report MIN-of-N (N=10 bench, N≥3 AT-1530).

**CpuFenceWall fallback:** when `timestampValidBits==0` OR `timestampPeriod==0` (e.g. Lavapipe), timing falls back to a CPU fence-wall measurement and `timing_source = CpuFenceWall`. This number INCLUDES submit + fence scheduling + driver overhead and is NOT a GPU kernel time. The bench/test MUST print timing_source and MUST NOT quote a CpuFenceWall number as a kernel-only figure. On this path NO query pool is created and NO vkCmdWriteTimestamp is recorded (recording a timestamp on a 0-valid-bits queue is a validation error).

### A. The three resident methods (impl VulkanContext, in resident.rs)

All three are inherent methods on `VulkanContext`. They REUSE existing machinery:
- buffer allocation: allocate_device_local_buffer, allocate_staging_buffer_cached, round_up_pow2 (buffers.rs)
- descriptor pool/set: allocate_descriptor_pool_and_set (kernel_handle.rs)
- binding plan + pipeline/layout: handle.inner pub(crate) fields
- timing math: masked_timestamp_delta (resident.rs, complete, AT-1535)
- workgroup guard: validate_request's workgroup check (dispatch.rs) / max_compute_work_group_count

#### upload_resident
```
pub fn upload_resident(
    &self,
    handle: &KernelHandle,
    inputs: &[&[u8]],
    output_sizes: &[u64],
) -> DispatchResult<ResidentBuffers>
```
Steps:
1. Validate inputs.len() and output_sizes.len() against handle.inner.binding_plan.buffers.len() (BindingCountMismatch — REUSE existing variant). Fail fast BEFORE any allocation (no leak).
2. For each binding i: size_needed = max(inputs[i].len(), output_sizes[i]).max(4), rounded via round_up_pow2. Allocate ONE device-local buffer. For OUTPUT (readback) bindings (binding_is_readback over access + output_size), also allocate a retained staging buffer for readback_resident. For INPUT upload, allocate a SEPARATE TRANSIENT staging buffer (NOT the retained one — OPT-NOTE-2: no aliasing with readback staging), copy_in the bytes, record a one-shot upload CB (transient staging→device-local copy + TRANSFER_WRITE→SHADER_READ barrier), submit on the compute queue UNDER queue_submit_lock, fence-wait, free the transient upload staging + transient CB/pool. This is the ONE-TIME upload; intentionally NOT in the timed loop.
3. Create a fresh descriptor pool + set via allocate_descriptor_pool_and_set(device, dsl, n_buffers). For 0-buffer kernels (n==0) descriptor_pool/descriptor_set = None. Write each device-local buffer into the set at binding index handle.inner.binding_plan.buffers[i].buffer_position (STORAGE_BUFFER, WHOLE_SIZE) — mirrors ensure_buffers_fit_with_mem_props rewrite loop.
4. Create the reusable command pool with RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER on the compute queue family, allocate ONE primary CB, create the reusable fence (unsignaled), and — ONLY IF select_timing_source(valid_bits, period)==GpuTimestamp — the 2-entry TIMESTAMP query pool (else query_pool = vk::QueryPool::null() and the CpuFenceWall path is used).
5. Snapshot timestamp_period, timestamp_valid_bits, queue_family_index into ResidentBuffers; uses_coopmat = false (diagnostic-only; handle carries no coopmat flag in M3.1.5 — FIELD-DOC-FIX).

**Partial-failure cleanup (CORRECTNESS-2):** build persistent objects into local Options; on ANY early-return Err after the first allocation, call `cleanup_partial_resident` which destroys (reverse creation order) whatever exists: query_pool, fence, command_pool, descriptor_pool, staging_bufs, device_local_bufs. The transient upload staging + transient CB/pool are freed on their own error paths (they are not ResidentBuffers fields). ResidentBuffers is constructed ONLY when ALL objects exist, so its Drop never double-frees.

#### dispatch_resident
```
pub fn dispatch_resident(
    &self,
    handle: &KernelHandle,
    resident: &ResidentBuffers,
    cfg: &ResidentBenchConfig,
) -> DispatchResult<ResidentDispatchTiming>
```
**CORRECTNESS-1 (guard FIRST):** build a transient DispatchRequest-equivalent or inline the workgroup check — call the existing workgroup-limit guard against self.max_compute_work_group_count() on cfg.workgroups[0..3]; on out-of-range return DispatchError::WorkgroupCountExceedsDeviceLimit { requested, max } BEFORE any GPU work. (Reuse the validate_request workgroup branch; the binding/push checks are already satisfied at upload time, so a minimal max-count check is sufficient — extract a small `fn workgroups_within_limit(wg, max) -> Result<(), DispatchError>` if cleaner.)

Decide timing source ONCE: `use_gpu_ts = select_timing_source(resident.timestamp_valid_bits, resident.timestamp_period) == GpuTimestamp` (and resident.query_pool != null). Steps (REUSE resident.command_buffer/fence/query_pool — no allocation):
1. reset_command_buffer(cb, empty). begin ONE_TIME_SUBMIT.
2. If use_gpu_ts: cmd_reset_query_pool(cb, query_pool, 0, 2) FIRST (HN-6: same submission, before any write), then cmd_write_timestamp(TOP_OF_PIPE, query_pool, 0).
3. cmd_bind_pipeline(COMPUTE, handle.inner.pipeline). If resident.descriptor_set Some: cmd_bind_descriptor_sets(COMPUTE, handle.inner.pipeline_layout, 0, [resident.descriptor_set], []) — bind the RESIDENT set, NOT handle.inner.descriptor_set. If cfg.push_constants non-empty: cmd_push_constants(handle.inner.pipeline_layout, COMPUTE, 0, &cfg.push_constants).
4. cmd_dispatch(cfg.workgroups). (No upload/readback copies.)
5. If use_gpu_ts: cmd_write_timestamp(BOTTOM_OF_PIPE, query_pool, 1).
6. end_command_buffer.
7. reset_fences([fence]). Take CPU t0 (Instant::now) BEFORE submit (for CpuFenceWall). Submit UNDER self.queue_submit_lock; release lock BEFORE wait_for_fences. wait_for_fences(AXC_FENCE_TIMEOUT_MS or DEFAULT_FENCE_TIMEOUT_MS); FenceTimeout on TIMEOUT.
8. kernel_ns:
   - GpuTimestamp: get_query_pool_results(query_pool, 0, &mut [u64;2], TYPE_64 | WAIT). ticks = masked_timestamp_delta(r0, r1, valid_bits). kernel_ns = (ticks as f64 * period as f64) as u64. source = GpuTimestamp.
   - CpuFenceWall: kernel_ns = t0.elapsed().as_nanos().min(u64::MAX as u128) as u64. source = CpuFenceWall.
Return ResidentDispatchTiming { kernel_ns, timing_source }.
Concurrency: &self + &ResidentBuffers; queue_submit_lock serializes the submit (CRITICAL-5 preserved). Caller MUST NOT call dispatch_resident on the SAME ResidentBuffers from two threads (shared CB/fence/query pool) — documented contract; bench is single-threaded.

#### readback_resident
```
pub fn readback_resident(
    &self,
    handle: &KernelHandle,
    resident: &ResidentBuffers,
    output_sizes: &[u64],
) -> DispatchResult<Vec<Vec<u8>>>
```
Precondition (OPT-NOTE-3): call AFTER upload → dispatch(s). Steps:
1. For each binding i: if NOT binding_is_readback -> push empty Vec (Lever A; staging_bufs[i] is None).
2. For readback slots: reset_command_buffer(cb) (cb is not in-flight — Drop/prior dispatch fence-waited), record a one-shot readback CB (device_local→staging copy + TRANSFER_WRITE→HOST_READ barrier), submit UNDER queue_submit_lock + fence-wait (separate submission; readback is NEVER timed). Invalidate the mapping if NonCoherent (mirror readback_from_persistent_mapping), then copy_out into a Vec<u8> of length output_sizes[i]. Return Vec<Vec<u8>> indexed by binding (empty for skipped).

### B. Dispatch-time preflight wiring (PREFLIGHT decision: additive)

Verified: prepare_kernel's signature is (spirv, binding_plan, push_constant_total_bytes, entry_point) and has NO coopmat shape / kernel_name. The coopmat REQUIRED SHAPE lives in KernelMetadata.coopmat. Folding the preflight INTO prepare_kernel would require ADDING coopmat+kernel_name params — a BREAKING signature change for every existing caller. Therefore the clean fix is an ADDITIVE checked wrapper:
```
pub fn prepare_kernel_checked(
    &self,
    spirv: &[u32],
    binding_plan: &ParamBindingPlan,
    push_constant_total_bytes: u32,
    entry_point: &str,
    coopmat: Option<&CoopMatShapeMeta>,
    kernel_name: &str,
) -> DispatchResult<KernelHandle>
```
It calls self.preflight_kernel_support(binding_plan, coopmat, kernel_name)? then self.prepare_kernel(...).

`preflight_kernel_support` (private):
1. required_device_features(binding_plan, coopmat.is_some()) vs self.enabled_features(): for each required-but-not-enabled feature (iterated in fixed declaration order of EnabledDeviceFeatures bools) -> Err(DeviceFeatureUnsupported { feature, kernel: kernel_name }).
2. If coopmat Some(meta): req = coopmat_required_shape_from_meta(meta). If !self.coopmat_support().feature_present OR !coopmat_shape_supported(&req, self.coopmat_support()) -> Err(CoopMatUnsupported { m/n/k from meta, reason }). If self.subgroup_size() != 32 -> Err(CoopMatUnsupported { ..., reason: 'subgroup size N != 32' }).
3. Else Ok(()).

**Honest gap statement:** prepare_kernel (unchecked) is RETAINED unchanged for back-compat; raw prepare_kernel callers remain UNPROTECTED by design. M3.1.5 SWITCHES the driver/bench/test paths to prepare_kernel_checked so the gap is exercised, but the milestone does NOT claim the gap is universally closed — it is 'closeable opt-in'. (A later milestone may store coopmat shape on KernelHandleInner to enable fold-in.)

### C. Benches (HONESTY-1, option b)

**Headline: `resident_timing_kernels`** — runs the resident path over EXISTING real kernels and reports HONEST kernel-only nanoseconds:
- saxpy (saxpy.axc), q4km matvec (q4km_dequant_matvec.axc), q4km matmul (q4km_dequant_matmul.axc): plain f32/quant kernels via prepare_kernel (or prepare_kernel_checked with coopmat=None — equivalent).
- coopmat matmul_tile (matmul_tile.axc) via prepare_kernel_checked; typed-skip on CoopMatUnsupported / subgroup!=32 (no crash).
For each: upload_resident once → 2 untimed warm-up dispatch_resident → N=10 measured → MIN-of-N kernel_ns → readback once (sanity). Prints `<kernel>: min kernel_ns = X (timing_source = GpuTimestamp|CpuFenceWall[— scheduling-inclusive, NOT a GPU kernel time])`. Asserts kernel_ns>0 && finite ONLY. NO TFLOPS, NO cuBLAS ratio.

**`naive_gemm_harness_validation`** (renamed from matmul_tflops_4096) — measures the NAIVE un-tiled scalar f32 GEMM (matmul_f32_tiled.axc, holes removed) via the resident path. Same warmup/min-of-N. Prints exactly: 'NAIVE un-tiled scalar f32 GEMM (harness validation only — NOT an optimized matmul; expect low single-digit % of cuBLAS; real tiling is M3.2): <tflops> TFLOPS (<pct>% of cuBLAS f32 datasheet ESTIMATE — not a same-machine A/B)'. Asserts ONLY tflops>0 && finite. Printed string MUST contain 'NAIVE' and 'harness validation' (AT-1581). wg_x for M·N/64: dispatch_resident's internal guard (CORRECTNESS-1) rejects out-of-range; the bench pre-shrinks M=N=K to the largest pow2 whose wg_x ≤ max_compute_work_group_count()[0], prints the ACTUAL dims, and asserts buffer total < 50 GB (4096² f32 ×3 ≈ 192 MB — fits; guard protects the shrink branch).

**`dispatch_resident_matmul_tile`** — switches to the resident API + prepare_kernel_checked preflight; typed-skip if coopmat/subgroup unsupported.

With the @strategy holes removed from matmul_f32_tiled.axc, ALL benches compile via the existing compile_source_with_meta — no compile_source_with_assignments needed (OPT-NOTE-1).

### D. panic -> typed error

design_md_additions:
## §3.1.13 (addendum, r1) — GPU-resident kernel-only timing METHODOLOGY (M3.1.5)

The thesis-relevant inference metric is resident throughput: weights/inputs are uploaded to device-local VRAM ONCE, then the kernel is dispatched many times; only the GPU-side dispatch is timed. M3.1.5 delivers this METHODOLOGY (not a competitive matmul number) via three additive inherent methods on `VulkanContext`:

- `upload_resident(handle, inputs, output_sizes) -> ResidentBuffers` — allocates device-local buffers, copies inputs in once (TRANSIENT staging CB, fence-waited; the retained per-slot staging is for READBACK only — no aliasing), builds a persistent descriptor set bound to those buffers (independent of the handle's dispatch_handle set), and creates a reusable command buffer + fence + (only on a timestamp-capable queue) a 2-entry query pool. On any partial-allocation failure it frees every already-created object before returning Err. The returned `ResidentBuffers` owns and (on Drop) frees all of these.
- `dispatch_resident(handle, &resident, cfg) -> ResidentDispatchTiming` — FIRST validates `cfg.workgroups` against `max_compute_work_group_count` (returns `WorkgroupCountExceedsDeviceLimit`), then records ONLY the compute submit into the reusable CB: (timestamp-capable path) `cmd_reset_query_pool` (same submission, HN-6) -> `write_timestamp(TOP_OF_PIPE)` -> bind pipeline/RESIDENT descriptor/push -> `dispatch` -> `write_timestamp(BOTTOM_OF_PIPE)`; submits under `queue_submit_lock`, fence-waits, and computes the GPU **dispatch duration** = `masked_timestamp_delta(t0,t1,valid_bits) * timestampPeriod`.
- `readback_resident(handle, &resident, output_sizes) -> Vec<Vec<u8>>` — copies device-local outputs to staging and out to host ONCE, after the dispatch loop (never timed). Readonly bindings are skipped (Lever A) and yield empty Vecs.

### Honest timing semantics

The measured quantity is the **GPU dispatch duration**: the TOP_OF_PIPE->BOTTOM_OF_PIPE timestamp span over the single dispatch. It EXCLUDES host upload (one-time, pre-loop) and readback (post-loop) — that exclusion is the entire value over `dispatch_handle` — but it INCLUDES dispatch launch and pipeline latency/drain. It is therefore NOT isolated ALU time and is not labeled 'kernel-only ALU'. Warmup-discard is mandatory (2 untimed dispatches discarded; report min-of-N). When the device reports `timestampValidBits==0` or `timestampPeriod==0` (e.g. Lavapipe), timing falls back to a CPU fence-wall measurement (`CpuFenceWall`) which INCLUDES submit + fence scheduling + driver overhead; this number is always reported with its `timing_source` and is NEVER quoted as a GPU kernel time.

### Dispatch-time safety

`prepare_kernel_checked` runs a typed preflight — `coopmat_shape_supported` + `subgroup_size()==32` + `required_device_features` vs `enabled_features` — returning `CoopMatUnsupported` / `DeviceFeatureUnsupported` (graceful skip) instead of crashing when a coopmat kernel meets an unsupported device. It is ADDITIVE: raw `prepare_kernel` callers remain unprotected by design (the coopmat shape is not in `prepare_kernel`'s signature); the runtime/driver/bench paths adopt the checked variant.

### First measured resident kernel-only timings

Reported as kernel-only **nanoseconds** (NOT extrapolated to a competitive TFLOPS) over EXISTING real kernels on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell:

> | kernel | min dispatch-span ns | timing_source |
> |---|---|---|
> | saxpy | <TODO measure> | GpuTimestamp |
> | q4km_dequant_matvec | <TODO> | GpuTimestamp |
> | q4km_dequant_matmul | <TODO> | GpuTimestamp |
> | matmul_tile (coopmat) | <TODO / skip if unsupported> | GpuTimestamp |

### Matmul TFLOPS is explicitly DEFERRED to M3.2

A competitive 4096² matmul TFLOPS headline is **NOT** in M3.1.5. A real tiled/coalesced matmul requires `shared[T,N]` workgroup memory (FG.6), which M3.2 delivers. The bundled `matmul_f32_tiled` is a NAIVE un-tiled scalar GEMM (one output element per invocation, uncoalesced B access) used ONLY for harness validation; its inert `@strategy{tile_m,tile_n}` holes were REMOVED (they were never wired into the kernel body, so they produced byte-identical SPIR-V). Any TFLOPS printed for it is labeled 'NAIVE un-tiled scalar f32 GEMM — harness validation only, NOT an optimized matmul; expect low single-digit % of cuBLAS; real tiling is M3.2'. The competitive A/B against llama.cpp uses a properly-tiled M3.2 kernel through this same resident-timing harness.
